title: Car window winder
prompt: A labelled teaching model of the 1998 page 39 manual car window winder has a hand crank, small cog, toothed quadrant, crossed lifting levers and glass guided in a tabletop frame. Wind up turns the cog and quadrant to raise the glass. Wind down reverses the drive and lowers it. Slow view slows the explanatory action. See-through exposes the crank connection, cog, quadrant teeth, lever pivots and sliding supports. A hand or teaching fixture supplies any required holding force. Do not claim the shown spur gears lock the window in place or add an unsourced brake or worm drive. Identify this as the 1998 manual-input variant, not the 2016 motor-driven diagram.
blurb: A 1998 manual-input teaching adaptation uses a hand crank, cog and quadrant to lift guided glass, with a teaching hand supplying the holding force.
adaptation: Crossed linkage in a tabletop frame with removable teaching covers and a holding hand. Spur gears are back-drivable. No brake or worm drive is represented.

editionAccess.2016: quadrant linkage corroboration only; motor-driven variant

truthNotes: Not an exact reconstruction or verified edition union.
The teaching hand remains on the crank and supplies holding torque.
Motion is geometrically constrained; tooth flanks are simplified teaching trapezoids.
